story_type: countdown hold seconds before a launch
hook: The last shuttle launch froze 31 seconds before liftoff.
narration: The last space shuttle launch ever froze thirty one seconds before liftoff.
July eighth, twenty eleven. Atlantis stood on the pad in Florida, ready to fly one last time.
At T minus thirty one seconds, the clock held.
A cap on top of the fuel tank had swung away. The switch that tells launch control it is safe never confirmed it.
So they checked the cap with a camera.
The cap was clear. Three main engines lit.
The final liftoff of Atlantis came just a few minutes late.
[short pause] Thirteen days later, it dropped out of the predawn dark toward Kennedy.
outcome: Atlantis landed at Kennedy for the final time, and the shuttle era was over.
title: Last shuttle launch froze at T-31
description:
On July 8, 2011, the countdown for STS-135, the final space shuttle mission, held at T minus 31 seconds when a switch failed to confirm a cap on the external tank had moved clear. A camera verified it, and Atlantis launched a few minutes late, then landed at Kennedy for the final time on July 21.
